title: Forty-four years, 35 moments
lede: From the predecessor’s incorporation to the one store still open, with the money and the rivals alongside. Filter by thread.

events.title: Predecessor incorporated
events.text: Blockbuster Entertainment Corporation is incorporated in Delaware. It enters the movie rental business three years later.

events.title: First store opens in Dallas
events.text: David Cook opens the first Blockbuster with some 8,000 tapes and a computerised checkout.

events.title: Huizenga’s group buys in
events.text: Cook sells part of the business to investors including Wayne Huizenga, leaves later that year, and the headquarters moves to Fort Lauderdale.

events.title: Largest chain in the country
events.text: About 400 stores.

events.title: Viacom merger announced
events.text: A merger valued at $8.4 billion, agreed while Viacom was bidding for Paramount.

events.title: Merger completed
events.text: Blockbuster Entertainment Corporation is merged into Viacom.

events.title: Revenue sharing with the studios
events.text: Instead of paying $60 to $70 a cassette, Blockbuster pays a small sum up front and shares rental income.

events.title: Initial public offering
events.text: 31 million class A shares are sold at $15, raising $465M. Viacom keeps control.

events.title: Late fees reach $692.6M
events.text: Extended viewing fees for 1999 are 15.5% of revenue.

events.title: Netflix asks $50M
events.text: By Marc Randolph’s account, Netflix’s founders propose a sale to Blockbuster in Dallas and are turned down.

events.title: Viacom decides to divest
events.text: Viacom announces it will pursue the divestiture of its approximately 81.5% stake.

events.title: Blockbuster Online launches
events.text: A DVD-by-mail subscription service in the United States, seven years after Netflix was founded.

events.title: $1.45B of new financing
events.text: A $1,150M senior secured credit facility and $300M of 9% senior subordinated notes.

events.title: $5.00 a share special distribution
events.text: About $905.6M in total is paid to shareholders ahead of the split-off.

events.title: Split-off from Viacom
events.text: Blockbuster becomes a fully independent company.

events.title: Peak: 9,094 stores
events.text: The highest year-end store count in the company’s history.

events.title: “The end of late fees”
events.text: Extended viewing fees end at more than 4,500 company stores and about 550 franchise stores. Items kept past a one-week grace period are sold to the customer.

events.title: Bid for Hollywood Video
events.text: Blockbuster offers $14.50 a share for Hollywood Entertainment. It lets the offer expire on March 24, citing antitrust clearance.

events.title: Movie Gallery buys Hollywood
events.text: The combined company has about 4,800 stores.

events.title: Icahn wins board seats
events.text: Carl Icahn, Edward Bleier and Strauss Zelnick are elected, replacing three incumbents including chairman John Antioco.

events.title: Netflix sues
events.text: Netflix files a patent suit over Blockbuster’s online service.

events.title: Total Access
events.text: Online subscribers can return mailed DVDs to a store and take a free rental. Subscribers pass 2 million by year-end.

events.title: Antioco’s exit agreed
events.text: A settlement over his 2006 bonus sets the end of his employment.

events.title: Jim Keyes becomes CEO
events.text: The former chief executive of 7-Eleven is named chairman and chief executive.

events.title: Kiosks with NCR
events.text: An agreement to put Blockbuster-branded vending kiosks in retail locations. There were 2,225 by January 2010.

events.title: Going-concern warning
events.text: The FY2009 annual report cites “substantial doubt” about the company’s ability to continue. It closed 374 U.S. stores in 2009.

events.title: Movie Gallery liquidates
events.text: The owner of Hollywood Video moves to close its remaining 1,900-plus stores.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Blockbuster Inc. and its U.S. subsidiaries file in the Southern District of New York, case 10-14997, with $125M of bankruptcy financing.

events.title: Dish wins the auction
events.text: Dish Network’s bid of about $320M is selected as the highest and best.

events.title: Sale closes at $320.6M
events.text: The estate expects about $226M net. Keyes and other executives are terminated the same day.

events.title: Dish closes the stores
events.text: The last 300 or so company-owned U.S. stores and the by-mail service are to shut by early January 2014.

events.title: Alaska stores close
events.text: The Bend, Oregon franchise becomes the last Blockbuster in the United States.

events.title: Perth closes
events.text: The Bend store becomes the last in the world.

events.title: The Last Blockbuster on Netflix
events.text: The documentary about the Bend store reaches the service that replaced it.

events.title: Still open
events.text: The Bend store’s website lists current releases. blockbuster.com shows the logo and a holding page.
